payload.title: Park uncommitted main changes and file tasks to land them
payload.description: Park the uncommitted changes on main onto a temp branch, work out why each change was made, group them into tasks, then work and land those tasks until main is clean.
payload.context: This repo is a dependency of Endless. Mike's goal (2026-10-17, during go-cliutil E-2289) is a clean set of Endless dependencies. Endless builds against this repo's working tree through a local replace, so check whether parking the changes breaks the Endless build first; if it does, the resulting tasks block whatever they would break.

fields.plan:
# Plan: Park uncommitted main changes and file tasks to land them

The main checkout of go-dt has uncommitted work (staged and unstaged) that predates this task. Endless and other repos build against that working tree through local `replace` directives. The goal is a clean main, with every change either landed through a task or deliberately dropped by Mike.

The changes at filing time (2026-10-17), excluding `.endless/`:
- Modified: path_segments_ext.go, dtx/test/go.mod.
- Untracked: dtx/go.sum.
- go-dt is foundational. go-cliutil, go-doterr's sync tool and Endless all depend on it, so check its importers when analyzing.

## Steps
1. **Snapshot without touching main.** From this task's worktree, read the main checkout's full diff against HEAD, staged and unstaged together, including deletions, binaries and untracked non-`.endless/` files. Recreate it on a branch named `wip/<task-id>` cut from main's HEAD, and commit it there as one commit with message "WIP snapshot of main working tree". Then confirm the branch's tree matches main's working tree file for file. Don't use `git stash`; the stash stack is shared across sessions.
2. **Analyze.** Go through the snapshot and work out why each change was made, from the code, nearby commits and other repos that depend on it. Group the changes into coherent units, such as "API rename following go-dt v0.5.0", "new feature X" or "dependency bumps". Flag anything that looks unfinished, accidental, or like a generated or binary artifact.
3. **Report to Mike before filing.** Show the grouping, what each group is for, and anything you couldn't explain, then let him adjust it.
4. **File one task per agreed group** in this project. Each plan names the files and hunks it takes from `wip/<task-id>`.
5. **Check whether Endless depends on the WIP.** Build Endless against this repo at main HEAD, without the WIP, using a scratch GOWORK that points this module at a clean checkout. Add blockers for whatever fails: each group whose removal breaks the build gets `--blocks` on the tasks that need it.
6. **Hand Mike one command to clear main's working tree.** He runs it himself, only after confirming `wip/<task-id>` holds everything. This session doesn't write to the main checkout.

## Done when
Every change in the snapshot belongs to a filed task or is listed as "drop" with Mike's agreement, main is clean, and any build dependency is recorded as a blocker.

fields.title: Tag new versions of go-dt's dtx, appinfo and dtglob
fields.description: Tag new versions of go-dt's dtx, appinfo and dtglob modules on published go-dt, with the Release workflow extended to make their directory-prefixed tags and the user told each tag and its reason
fields.plan:
## Approach

**Modules.** In dtx, appinfo and dtglob, drop the `replace github.com/mikeschinkel/go-dt => ../` line, then with `GOWORK=off` run `go get github.com/mikeschinkel/go-dt@v0.6.1` and `go mod tidy` so go.mod and go.sum name the published version. In each test and example module, keep only the replace pointing at the module under test (`dtx/test`: `dtx => ..`; `test` and `examples/basic_usage`: `go-dt => ..` / `../..`), drop any other, and tidy with `GOWORK=off`. dtx, appinfo and dtglob each depend only on root, so they have no order among themselves.

**Local development.** Convert the Makefile to a justfile recipe for recipe (help, test, test-unit, test-corpus, test-all, lint, fmt, vet, tidy, build, examples, clean, ci, ensure-valid), keeping `GOEXPERIMENT=jsonv2`. Add `work`, which runs `go work init` over every directory holding a go.mod (removing an existing go.work first). go.work and go.work.sum stay gitignored. Add a README section on local development covering `just work`, why go.work is not committed, and `GOWORK=off`.

**test.yml.** Set `GOWORK: off` at workflow level. Keep the root unit, fuzz-corpus and lint jobs; add a step per nested module that tests it and its test module; add a `go mod tidy -diff` check over every module.

**release.yml.** Replace the free-text `version` input with a `module` choice input (root, dtx, appinfo, dtglob) and a `version` input validated as `vX.Y.Z[-pre]`. Compute `TAG` and `DIR` from them. Before tagging: check `$DIR/go.mod` declares the module path for `$DIR` and contains no replace; run the module's tests (and its test module's) with `GOWORK=off`. Take `PREV_TAG` from `git tag -l "<prefix>v*" --sort=-v:refname` (root: tags without a slash). Build notes from `git log PREV_TAG..HEAD -- $DIR` (root: excluding the nested module directories). Title the release with the module name.

**Versions.** For each of dtx, appinfo and dtglob, compare its exported API at its last tag against HEAD (`go doc -all` or apidiff in a scratch copy). Per Go Stability at v0: a removal or incompatible change is a minor bump, otherwise patch. Give the user each tag, the reason and a short description, and wait for them to run the workflow.

**Gomion and Endless.** Add an open question to gomion E-2434, E-2212 and E-2347 and endless E-2433: whether release tooling should rely on go.work plus no replace in publishable modules, instead of removing and restoring replaces. Cite the trial results recorded in this task's analysis.
fields.analysis:
## Why go.work instead of replace in publishable modules

A replace in a published module is ignored by consumers, so its require is the only thing a consumer sees, while locally the replace makes that require irrelevant. Nothing forces the number to be correct. Today's dtx shows it: built against its stated require (go-dt v0.5.0) it fails with `undefined: dt.ErrFileNotExist` and `undefined: dt.Logf`. go.work gives the same local behaviour (all modules built from disk) without touching go.mod, and since it is not committed, CI builds against the requires.

A replace is still correct in a module that is never published and exists to test the code in the same commit: without one, CI would test dtx/test against the published dtx. Keeping only the replace to the tested module means CI tests the commit's dtx, built against the go-dt version dtx itself requires.

## Trial (scratch copy of main, Go 1.26.2)

- All replaces removed, go.work over all nine modules: every module vets and tests. dtglob/test failed only because its own replace had been removed too and it requires dtglob at the zero pseudo-version; with its replace kept, it passes.
- Root and dtx changed together (dtx using a new root function): builds locally under go.work; with GOWORK=off and dtx requiring v0.6.1 it fails `undefined: dt.TrialHello`, so CI catches unpublished dependencies.
- GOWORK=off with requires bumped to v0.6.1 and go mod tidy: dtx, appinfo, dtglob, test and examples vet clean. Without the tidy, go.sum lacks go-dt's checksums (never recorded, because of the replace).
- dtx left out of go.work: go refuses loudly ("directory prefix . does not contain modules listed in go.work").
- dtx/test keeping `replace dtx => ..` alongside go.work: no conflict; GOWORK=off sees the commit's dtx.
- An outside consumer requiring dtx/v0.2.1 and go-dt v0.6.1 fails `undefined: dt.ErrFileDoesNotExist` (renamed in v0.6.0): what blocks go-cliutil.

## Rejected

- Committing go.work with GOWORK=off in every workflow: a step that forgets it silently builds against disk code.
- A committed go.local-dev.work copied by a recipe: must be edited when modules are added; generating from the go.mod files needs no upkeep. Endless E-1192 (go.work generation tool) can replace the recipe later.
- Free-text tag input: a typo fails only after starting the run; a module choice makes the tag and directory unable to disagree.
- CI running go mod tidy for you: CI must test what is committed; it checks tidiness and fails instead.

ops.statement: README.md documents that local development needs a go.work, created by running just work

fields.plan:
## Approach

**Modules.** In dtx, appinfo and dtglob, drop the `replace github.com/mikeschinkel/go-dt => ../` line, then with `GOWORK=off` run `go get github.com/mikeschinkel/go-dt@v0.6.1` and `go mod tidy` so go.mod and go.sum name the published version. In each test and example module, keep only the replace pointing at the module under test (`dtx/test`: `dtx => ..`; `test` and `examples/basic_usage`: `go-dt => ..` / `../..`), drop any other, and tidy with `GOWORK=off`. dtx, appinfo and dtglob each depend only on root, so they have no order among themselves.

**Local development.** Convert the Makefile to a justfile recipe for recipe (help, test, test-unit, test-corpus, test-all, lint, fmt, vet, tidy, build, examples, clean, ci, ensure-valid), keeping `GOEXPERIMENT=jsonv2`. Add `work`, which runs `go work init` over every directory holding a go.mod (removing an existing go.work first). go.work and go.work.sum stay gitignored. Add a README section on local development covering `just work`, why go.work is not committed, and `GOWORK=off`.

**test.yml.** Set `GOWORK: off` at workflow level. Keep the root unit, fuzz-corpus and lint jobs; add a step per nested module that tests it and its test module; add a `go mod tidy -diff` check over every module.

**release.yml.** Replace the free-text `version` input with a `module` choice input (root, dtx, appinfo, dtglob) and a `version` input validated as `vX.Y.Z[-pre]`. Compute `TAG` and `DIR` from them. Before tagging: check `$DIR/go.mod` declares the module path for `$DIR` and contains no replace; run the module's tests (and its test module's) with `GOWORK=off`. Take `PREV_TAG` from `git tag -l "<prefix>v*" --sort=-v:refname` (root: tags without a slash). Build notes from `git log PREV_TAG..HEAD -- $DIR` (root: excluding the nested module directories). Title the release with the module name.

**Versions.** For each of dtx, appinfo and dtglob, compare its exported API at its last tag against HEAD (`go doc -all` or apidiff in a scratch copy). Per Go Stability at v0: a removal or incompatible change is a minor bump, otherwise patch. Give the user each tag, the reason and a short description, and wait for them to run the workflow.

**Gomion and Endless.** Add an open question to gomion E-2434, E-2212 and E-2347 and endless E-2433: whether release tooling should rely on go.work plus no replace in publishable modules, instead of removing and restoring replaces. Cite the trial results recorded in this task's analysis.

**Verify suite.** Copy `_harness.sh` and `_guard.sh` verbatim from Endless's `.endless/tasks/` into go-dt's `.endless/tasks/`, and write E-2431's suite as `.endless/tasks/e-2431/verify.sh` sourcing the harness. Each module is checked with `cd <dir> && GOWORK=off go ...`, since a gotest check cannot reach a nested module (endless E-2438).

fields.analysis:
Two shapes were considered. (1) A language-agnostic check field naming the directory a check runs in (e.g. dir), honoured by every driver, generic sh checks included. (2) A field the language driver declares and consumes, like gotest's existing tests and paths, which the Check type already accepts only on structured drivers (e.g. module on gotest).

Mike, 2026-10-25: dir sounds like a good generic solution however runner-specific fields are handled.

Open point raised with it: what happens when two runners each want a runner-specific field of the same name (e.g. Go and Python both wanting module)? Fields are per check, and each [[check]] names one runner, so the two never meet in one table and each runner reads its own. The cost is meaning, not collision: Go's module would be a directory while Python's is a dotted import name, and Check is one flat struct, so one TOML key would carry two meanings, validated per driver. Ways to settle it when planning: share a key name across runners only when its meaning is the same, or put runner-specific fields in a per-runner subtable (e.g. [check.gotest]) so each runner owns its own namespace.
